The '''56th Academy Awards''' ceremony, presented by the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] (AMPAS), honored the best [[1983 in film|films of 1983]] and took place on April 9, 1984, at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in [[Los Angeles]], beginning at 6:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] / 9:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]]. During the ceremony, AMPAS presented [[Academy Awards]] (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 22 categories. The ceremony, televised in the United States by [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], was produced by [[Jack Haley Jr.]] and directed by [[Marty Pasetta]].<ref name="Pasetta">{{harvnb|Osborne|1999|p=341}}</ref> Comedian and talk show emcee Johnny Carson hosted the show for the fifth time. He first presided over the [[51st Academy Awards|51st ceremony]] held in 1979 and last hosted the [[54th Academy Awards|54th ceremony]] held in 1982.<ref>{{cite web |last=Steinberg |first=David |title=The Gold Standard |url=https://www.latimes.com/la-mag-feb082009-theear-story.html |url-access=limited |access-date=March 23, 2020 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=January 30, 2009 |archive-date=April 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200404051915/https://www.latimes.com/la-mag-feb082009-theear-story.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Nine days earlier, in a ceremony held at [[The Beverly Hilton]] in [[Beverly Hills, California]], on March 31, the [[Academy Scientific and Technical Awards]] were presented by hosts [[Joan Collins]] and [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Past Scientific & Technical Awards Ceremonies |url=http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html |access-date=July 31, 2013 |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140213185729/http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html |archive-date=February 13, 2014}}</ref>

''[[Terms of Endearment]]'' won five awards, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Harmetz |first=Aljean |title='Terms' Wins Best Picture; Duvall and Miss MacLaine Honored |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/04/10/movies/terms-wins-best-picture-oscar-duvall-and-miss-maclaine-honored.html |access-date=June 29, 2020 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=April 10, 1984 |archive-date=June 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629192300/https://www.nytimes.com/1984/04/10/movies/terms-wins-best-picture-oscar-duvall-and-miss-maclaine-honored.html |url-access=limited |url-status=live}}</ref> Other winners included ''[[Fanny and Alexander]]'' and ''[[The Right Stuff (film)|The Right Stuff]]'' with four awards, ''[[Tender Mercies]]'' with two awards, and ''[[Return of the Jedi]]'', ''[[Boys and Girls (1983 film)|Boys and Girls]]'', ''[[Flamenco at 5:15]]'', ''[[Flashdance]]'', ''[[He Makes Me Feel Like Dancin']]'', ''[[Sundae in New York]]'', ''[[The Year of Living Dangerously (film)|The Year of Living Dangerously]]'', and ''[[Yentl (film)|Yentl]]'' with one. The telecast garnered 42.1&nbsp;million viewers in the United States.

==Winners and nominees==
The nominees for the 56th Academy Awards were announced on February 16, 1984, by Academy president [[Gene Allen (art director)|Gene Allen]] and actor [[Mickey Rooney]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Oscar Nominations Are Due |work=[[Baytown Sun]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/83350953/oscar-nominations-are-due/ |access-date=July 12, 2021 |date=February 16, 1984 |page=2-A |publisher=[[Newspapers.com]] |archive-date=August 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210813083114/https://www.newspapers.com/clip/83350953/oscar-nominations-are-due/ |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Terms of Endearment]]'' earned the most nominations with eleven; ''[[The Right Stuff (film)|The Right Stuff]]'' came in second with eight.<ref>{{cite web |last=Harmetz |first=Aljean |author-link=Aljean Harmetz |title='Endearment' Tops Oscar Nominations |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/02/17/movies/endearment-tops-oscar-nominations.html |access-date=June 29, 2020 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=February 17, 1984 |archive-date=July 1, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170701012308/http://www.nytimes.com/1984/02/17/movies/endearment-tops-oscar-nominations.html |url-status=live |url-access=limited}}</ref> The winners were announced at the awards ceremony on April 9. [[James L. Brooks]] was the third writer-director-producer to win three Oscars for the same film.<ref>{{harvnb|Jones|1999|p=250}}</ref> With four wins, ''[[Fanny and Alexander]]'' became the [[List of Academy Award–winning foreign-language films|most awarded foreign language film]] in Academy Award history at the time.<ref name="HonoraryOscars">{{harvnb|Kinn|Piazza|2002|p=237}}</ref>{{efn|name=Fanny|''[[Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon]]'' (2000), ''[[Parasite (2019 film)|Parasite]]'' (2019), and ''[[All Quiet on the Western Front (2022 film)|All Quiet on the Western Front]]'' (2022) have since equaled this record with four wins apiece.<ref>{{cite web |last=Seibold |first=Witney |title='All Quiet on the Western Front's Oscar-Nominated Screenplay Was Kept Alive by Triathlons |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1231758/all-quiet-on-the-western-fronts-oscar-nominated-screenplay-was-kept-alive-by-triathlons/ |access-date=July 18, 2024 |work=[[/Film]] |date=March 17, 2023 |archive-date=March 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230327020529/https://www.slashfilm.com/1231758/all-quiet-on-the-western-fronts-oscar-nominated-screenplay-was-kept-alive-by-triathlons/ |url-status=live}}</ref>}} [[Linda Hunt]] is the only person to win an Oscar for playing a character of the opposite sex.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=1145}}</ref> Best Original Song co-winner [[Irene Cara]] became the first black woman to win an Oscar in a non-acting category.<ref>{{cite web |last=Scott |first=Mike |title=It Was a Big Night for 'Green Book'; It Was a Bigger One for the N.O. Film Industry |url=https://www.nola.com/entertainment_life/article_0453dd3e-719b-58aa-947d-2257fdd1cb23.html |access-date=April 25, 2021 |work=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate|The Times-Picayune]] |date=February 25, 2019 |archive-date=July 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210712091635/https://www.nola.com/entertainment_life/article_0453dd3e-719b-58aa-947d-2257fdd1cb23.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Honorary Award ===

==Ceremony information==
[[File:Johnny Carson 1970.JPG|thumb|left|alt=Johnny Carson in 1970|[[Johnny Carson]] hosted the 56th Academy Awards.]]
In September 1983, the Academy hired film producer [[Jack Haley Jr.]] to produce the telecast for the third time.<ref>{{cite news |last=Anderson |first=George |title=Triangle Tattler: 'Cats', 'Dreamgirls,' '42nd Street' to Tour |work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |date=September 20, 1984 |page=24}}</ref> "We are excited to have Jack Haley Jr. back on the Academy Awards program this year," said AMPAS President Gene Allen in a press release announcing the selection. "We know that his outstanding talents will ensure an innovative and entertaining approach to the presentation of the Oscar."<ref>{{cite web |title=Jack Haley Jr. to Produce the 56th Academy Awards Show |url=https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/7985/rec/13 |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |access-date=July 29, 2021 |page=1 |date=September 12, 1983 |archive-date=July 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729082044/https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/7985/rec/13 |url-status=live}}</ref> That same month, it was announced that comedian and ''[[The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson|The Tonight Show Starring]]'' host [[Johnny Carson]] would preside over emceeing duties for the 1984 ceremony. Allen explained the decision to hire Carson, saying, "In past years, Johnny has been a vital element in the ever-increasing success and popularity of the Oscar presentations. We are extremely pleased that we will be able to draw once again on his wit and charisma to host this special entertainment event."<ref>{{cite news |title=People: Here's Johnny Once Again on Oscar Show |work=[[Akron Beacon Journal]] |date=September 11, 1983 |page=2}}</ref>

Several other people were involved with the production of the ceremony. Musician [[Quincy Jones]] served as musical director for the ceremony, where he conducted an overture performed by the orchestra at the beginning of the show.<ref>{{cite news |last=Shull |first=Richard K. |title=Oscars Not So Endearing |page=15 |work=[[The Indianapolis News]] |date=April 10, 1984}}</ref> Former child actress [[Shirley Temple]] made a special appearance at the beginning of the telecast to discuss her memories of the [[7th Academy Awards|7th ceremony]] in 1935, where she received the [[Academy Juvenile Award]].<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=639}}</ref> Singers [[Sammy Davis Jr.]] and [[Liza Minnelli]] performed "[[There's No Business Like Show Business]]" at the conclusion of the telecast.<ref name="Gag">{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=641}}</ref> [[Marty Pasetta]] served as director for the telecast.<ref name="Pasetta"/> Notably, this was the first Oscars ceremony where the voting rules were announced at the end of the telecast as opposed to the beginning.<ref name="Gag"/>

===Box office performance of Best Picture nominees===
At the time of the nominations announcement on February 16, the combined gross of the five Best Picture nominees at the US box office was $151 million.<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars>{{cite web |title=1983 Academy Award Nominations and Winner for Best Picture |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1983&p=.htm |access-date=June 17, 2014 |publisher=[[Box Office Mojo]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140614052200/http://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1983&p=.htm |archive-date=June 14, 2014}}</ref> ''Terms of Endearment'' was the highest earner among the Best Picture nominees, with $72.9&nbsp;million in domestic box office receipts. The film was followed by ''The Big Chill'' ($52.5&nbsp;million), ''The Right Stuff'' ($15.7&nbsp;million), ''Tender Mercies'' ($8.44&nbsp;million), and ''The Dresser'' ($562,623).<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars/>

===Critical reviews===
Columnist Jerry Coffey from the ''[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]'' wrote, "Nothing that goes on during an Oscarcast is worth the tedium dumbly endured by the ever-gullible audience for moviedom's annual spasm of gross self-indulgence."<ref>{{cite web |last=Coffey |first=Jerry |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/83351171/gullible-viewers-hooked-again-by/ |title=Gullible Viewers Hooked Again by Tedious Academy Awards |work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |date=April 11, 1984 |access-date=August 26, 2020 |page=7D |via=Newspapers.com |archive-date=August 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210813083114/https://www.newspapers.com/clip/83351171/gullible-viewers-hooked-again-by/ |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Austin American-Statesman]]'' film critic Patrick Taggart commented, "By now after a week after the fact, it is a matter of record that Monday's Academy Awards show was without the dullest ever." He added, "The Oscar went to the predictable choice in every case, and not only were there no surprises among the awards, there weren't even any of those deliciously embarrassing moments that make live television what it is."<ref>{{cite web |last=Taggart |first=Patrick |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/83351179/unrewarding-oscar-shows-bright-spots/ |title=Unrewarding: Oscar Show's Bright Spots Few and Far Between |work=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |access-date=May 28, 2021 |date=April 15, 1984 |page=221 |via=Newspapers.com |archive-date=August 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210813083116/https://www.newspapers.com/clip/83351179/unrewarding-oscar-shows-bright-spots/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Television critic [[Howard Rosenberg]] of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' noted, "Be honest. This was not one of your more electrifying Academy Awards telecasts. The three hours and 40 minutes passed as swiftly as ''[[Barry Lyndon]]''." He also said, "And the tradition of squeezing nearly all of the major, most glamorous awards into the last half hour again proved mistaken, ill conceived, and just plain dumb."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://latimes.newspapers.com/newspage/390910976/ |access-date=April 12, 2026 |last=Rosenberg |first=Howard |author-link=Howard Rosenberg |title=It Was Not an Endearing Oscarcast |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=April 11, 1984 |page=85 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

Other media outlets received the broadcast more positively. Television columnist [[John J. O'Connor (journalist)|John J. O'Connor]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' wrote, "The tone of the proceedings was set and maintained by a spiritedly genial Mr. Carson." He also added that Carson was able to "provide with eternally boyish grace his typical comedy mix."<ref>{{cite web |last=O'Connor |first=John J. |title=Oscar Program: Long, But Different |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/04/11/arts/tv-review-oscar-program-different-but-long.html |url-access=limited |access-date=February 29, 2020 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=April 11, 1984 |archive-date=July 19, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210719092738/https://www.nytimes.com/1984/04/11/arts/tv-review-oscar-program-different-but-long.html |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[The Baltimore Sun]]'' film critic Stephen Hunter quipped, "The show, one of the crispest and most swiftly-paced in recent years, enjoyed its greatest asset in the return of Johnny Carson to the role of master of ceremonies. Mr. Carson was in top form."<ref>{{cite web |last=Hunter |first=Stephen |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/83350915/endearment-wins-oscars-as-best-picture/ |title='Endearment' Wins Oscars as Best Picture |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |access-date=November 19, 2020 |date=April 10, 1984 |pages=A8 |via=Newspapers.com |archive-date=August 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210813083115/https://www.newspapers.com/clip/83350915/endearment-wins-oscars-as-best-picture/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Mike Duffy of the ''[[Detroit Free Press]]'' wrote, "Johnny Carson, once again the invaluable host, added some much needed spice with well-timed zingers. And I especially enjoyed Jack Nicholson's impersonation of a [[The Blues Brothers|Blues Brother]] behind those black be-bopper shades."<ref>{{cite web |last=Duffy |first=Mike |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/83351193/sure-they-drag-but-the-oscars-are/ |title=Sure They Drag, but The Oscars Are Always Fun |page=9D |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=April 11, 1984 |via=Newspapers.com |access-date=July 28, 2021 |archive-date=August 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210813083116/https://www.newspapers.com/clip/83351193/sure-they-drag-but-the-oscars-are/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Ratings and reception===
The American telecast on [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] drew in an average of 42.1&nbsp;million people over the length of the entire ceremony, which was a 21% decrease from the [[55th Academy Awards|previous year's ceremony]].<ref name=var1>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2012/tv/news/crystal-social-media-fuel-oscar-ratings-1118050758/ |title=Crystal, social media fuel Oscar ratings |last=Kissell |first=Rick |date=February 27, 2012 |access-date=April 26, 2012 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130926040411/http://variety.com/2012/tv/news/crystal-social-media-fuel-oscar-ratings-1118050758/ |archive-date=September 26, 2013}}</ref> Moreover, the show drew lower [[Nielsen ratings]] compared to the previous ceremony, with 30.3% of households watching with a 50% share.<ref>{{cite news |title=Nielsen Ratings |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=April 18, 1984 |pages=E12}}</ref> Nevertheless, the ceremony presentation received four nominations at the [[36th Primetime Emmy Awards]] in August 1984.<ref>{{cite web |title=The 56th Annual Academy Awards–Emmy Awards, Nominations and Wins |url=https://www.emmys.com/shows/56th-annual-academy-awards |publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts and Sciences]] |access-date=November 16, 2020 |archive-date=March 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303215809/https://www.emmys.com/shows/56th-annual-academy-awards |url-status=live}}</ref> The following month, the ceremony won one of those nominations for Outstanding Art Direction for a Variety Program (Roy Christopher).<ref>{{cite web |last=Margulies |first=Lee |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/83351226/first-round-emmys-presented-moyers/ |title=First-Round Emmys Presented: Moyers' 'Walk', J.F.K. Special Honored |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=September 19, 1984 |page=I10 |via=Newspapers.com |access-date=May 23, 2021 |archive-date=August 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210813083114/https://www.newspapers.com/clip/83351226/first-round-emmys-presented-moyers/ |url-status=live}}</ref>
